name: Speak 714
label: Revelation
lede: Joe Foster turned up with five songs already recorded, Dan O'Mahony sang them with his jaw wired shut, and Revelation had the record out inside the year. Speak 714 lasted about as long as the paperwork.

eras.title: Five songs, a tattoo and a wired jaw
eras.text: Joe Foster of Ignite and Unity went to Dan O'Mahony, ex-No For An Answer and 411, with music already on tape. Players from Pennywise, Straight Faced and Slapshot filled out the record, and the band spent a year on the road.

years.cap: Speak 714 live at Worcester Artists Group, Massachusetts
years.h: Joe Foster shows up with five songs already recorded
years.p: Foster, the Ignite guitarist, brings the tapes to O'Mahony and builds a band around them: Pennywise's Randy Bradbury, Straight Faced's Sam Marrs, and Doug McKinnon of Slapshot and [[The Vandals|f54fc7c3-3a40-4f26-83cf-328d9b097e93]] on drums.
years.xp: O'Mahony told No Echo the material was "what the follow up to Unity's You Are One EP should have been." He had just moved back to Southern California when Foster got in touch.

years.big: To this day you will never hear me include the '714'
years.h: The name was taken twice, so the area code went on
years.p: O'Mahony, quoted in 2025. The band started as Thirst, became Speak after his forearm tattoo, and added the Orange County area code once Speak turned out to be taken too.
years.xp:
Thirst went first, after another band turned up holding the name. Speak was the replacement, taken from the tattoo on O'Mahony's left forearm.

By then manufacturing had started on the record. Someone else already had Speak, so 714 went on the sleeve, and O'Mahony has been dropping it in conversation ever since.

years.cap: Speak 714 live at Infinity, Springfield, Massachusetts, 1998
q: a Las Vegas brawl that didn't exactly go my way
years.h: A Las Vegas fight wires O'Mahony's jaw shut
years.p: Before Knee Deep in Guilt is finished, O'Mahony's jaw is broken in a fight he says didn't go his way. He can't record vocals with it wired, so the album waits six weeks.
years.xp: The one-line version from O'Mahony is "a Las Vegas brawl that didn't exactly go my way." The six-week delay is the only cost he puts on it.

years.src: Visions · Revelation Records: pressing history · No Echo: Speak 714
years.h: Revelation puts out Knee Deep in Guilt as REV 64
years.p: Ten songs in about 21 minutes, co-produced by O'Mahony and Foster. Germany's Visions called it a really great record and hoped the band would last.
years.xp: Revelation's first vinyl run was 110 copies on tan. In Europe the record came out through SPV.

years.cap: Speak 714 live at Infinity, Springfield, Massachusetts, 1998
years.h: Speak 714 spend the year on the road
years.p: Two US tours and a European one fit into the same year. O'Mahony calls the headlining runs in the States and Europe a privilege.
years.xp: O'Mahony described it as "some of the heaviest roadwork I've ever done." Fan footage survives from two US dates: Princeton Arts Council on May 16 and the Fireside Bowl in Chicago on July 21, 1998.

years.h: Live at the Princeton Arts Council, May 16, 1998
yt: Live at the Princeton Arts Council, May 16, 1998

eras.title: Same singer, new players
eras.text: Dan O'Mahony and Joe Foster stopped getting along, and the original band went with it. O'Mahony made one more record as Speak 714 with a new line-up, and the band wound down after that.

years.src: No Echo: Speak 714 · Revelation Records: pressing history · Discogs: The Scum Also Rises
years.h: The Scum Also Rises arrives with a new band behind O'Mahony
years.p: After O'Mahony and Foster split, Chris Lisk, Kevin Panter, Eryc Simmerer and Jeff Baker play on the EP. Simmerer wrote the music for Amsterdam.
years.xp:
O'Mahony says the friction with Foster led to a complete line-up change, and he came out of the EP friends with Lisk, Panter and Simmerer. Revelation pressed the first run on yellow vinyl, 180 copies, as REV 72.

There was no last show. In O'Mahony's words the band went through "gradual disintegration after a year plus of hitting things really hard."

eras.title: Done Dying instead of a reunion
eras.text: Speak 714 never came back. O'Mahony and Doug McKinnon kept playing together, in Done Dying and later Shiners Club.

years.src: No Echo: Interview with Dan O'Mahony
years.h: O'Mahony and McKinnon start Done Dying
years.p: The Speak 714 singer and drummer form Done Dying. O'Mahony describes it as a band of reunion-age players refusing to be a reunion band.
years.xp: The band has been trying to go full-time since 2013, and O'Mahony calls it the most fun he's had in a band. He told No Echo he hopes Done Dying has one more LP left in it.

years.h: Asked about a Speak 714 reunion, O'Mahony sees little demand
years.p: In 2025 O'Mahony says the inspiration would have to be there, and that he can't imagine much demand.
years.xp: His answer to No Echo, in full: "Hard to say. The inspiration to do so matters." The demand part came after.
